body: I have just finished a small html5 game using Websockets in 4.4.dev4 and was able to connect to a windows and linux server without issues.
The problems is happening when I connect to a Golang websocket server using the Melody framework, are you connecting to a godot websocket server?

Experiencing the same issue here in Godot 4.4 dev 4+ when connecting to a Golang websocket server using the Gorilla framework.

I found that if the server is running on port 443, and the port number is either omitted from, or set to 443 in the url string in the `WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url` method, it works fine. But any other port does not work.

I can also confirm that downgrading my project to 4.4 dev 3, without any code changes on the server or client, solves the issue, so it definitely appears to be an issue with the dev 4+ export.

Edit: not sure if Golang is a red herring, just thought I'd mention in case it's relevant. I have not tested with a different server.
The error apears to happen exclusively when connecting to a url different to the default port 80

I'm running into basically the same problem with 4.2.1.  I have a twitch chat viewer that will connect to the eventsub using websockets, and if the connection drops for some reason, it won't reconnect without completely restarting the application.  Seems to be perpetually stuck in "connecting".  I create a completely new WebSocket, and the error code returned is 0, so it should be good:
```gdscript
	eventsub_websocket = WebSocketPeer.new()
	var err = eventsub_websocket.connect_to_url(url)
```

Kind of curious if this is a long term issue that somehow comes and goes on a regression that happened between recent versions.  I'll have to to do some more testing to see what versions my issue occurs on.
@AThousandShips should this be tagged as a regression?
Not confirmed as a regression, it happens in 4.2.1 so doesn't seem like a regression

It could be a regression that happened between 4.4-dev3 and 4.4-dev4 as OP suggests, or maybe 4.3 and 4.4-dev4.  I haven't tested my project with those builds.  My issue could also be slightly different.  Unfortunately, OBS is using the wrong window for the overlay in 4.3 and newer, so I've had to stick with 4.2 for this project.  I think that's an OBS bug, not a Godot bug, though.
